svg.title: Cook’s Claim, The First Fleet Voyage & Founding of Sydney Cove (1770–1792)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 8 historical GIS two-panel atlas map showing Captain Cook and Tupaia’s 1770 East Coast claim from Kamay (Botany Bay) to Possession Island alongside Arthur Phillip’s 15,000-mile First Fleet convict voyage (May 1787 – January 1788) from Portsmouth via Tenerife, Rio de Janeiro, and Cape Town to Port Jackson, paired with a zoomed 1:10m GIS inset of Eora and Dharug Country, Kamay (Botany Bay), Warrane (Sydney Cove), Parramatta, and the Hawkesbury–Nepean frontier.

g.text: ZOOM: EORA COUNTRY, KAMAY (BOTANY BAY) & SYDNEY BASIN (1770–92)

under false claim of terra nullius

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 8 ENQUIRY: FIRST NATIONS & COLONIAL AUSTRALIA
Cook’s Claim, The First Fleet Voyage & Founding of Sydney Cove (1770–1792)
Losing America (1783) filled Britain’s Thames prison hulks, driving Arthur Phillip’s 15,000-mile First Fleet voyage to New South Wales.
Moving from Kamay (Botany Bay) to Warrane (Sydney Cove) under terra nullius sparked smallpox devastation and Eora resistance.
